content: Before starting mifepristone and each time you receive a refill, carefully read the medication guide provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally with a meal as directed by your doctor, typically once daily. Swallow the tablets whole without crushing or chewing them. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, nonprescription drugs, and herbal products. To minimize the risk of side effects, your doctor may recommend starting with a low dose and gradually increasing it. Use this medication consistently to achieve the maximum benefit. Do not discontinue this medication unless instructed by your doctor. If the medication is stopped, you may need to restart at a lower dose and gradually increase it again. Avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while taking this medication unless your doctor or pharmacist confirms it is safe to do so. Grapefruit can increase the likelihood of side effects associated with this medication. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, dry mouth, fatigue, dizziness, headache, or joint and muscle pain. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, this medication can cause low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Symptoms of low blood sugar include sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands or feet. It is advisable to carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar. If these are unavailable, quickly raise your blood sugar by consuming a fast source of sugar, such as sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. Notify your doctor immediately about the reaction and the use of this product. Symptoms of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) include increased thirst and urination. If these symptoms occur, inform your doctor immediately. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking mifepristone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Mifepristone may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Mifepristone must not be used during pregnancy, as it may result in pregnancy loss. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Mifepristone can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Similarly, other medications can influence the removal of mifepristone from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss non-hormonal birth control methods with your doctor or pharmacist while using this medication. Beta-blocker medications (such as metoprolol, propranolol, or glaucoma eye drops like timolol) may prevent the fast or pounding heartbeat typically associated with low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Many drugs can affect your blood sugar levels, making it harder to control. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist about how the medication may affect your blood sugar. Regularly monitor your blood sugar levels as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high or low blood sugar. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as potassium levels, thyroid function, and blood pressure) should be conducted. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
